subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What permanent API shape should OpenClaw expose for Telegram custom emoji delivery: a portable rich-text/custom-emoji representation, raw Telegram `entities` and `caption_entities`, or Telegram-only channel data?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix expands shared message-tool or Telegram channel-data API shape and affects plugin contracts rather than repairing one private implementation branch.

options.title: Design Shared Rich-Text Entity API
options.body: Add a typed representation that can carry custom emoji IDs through the shared message tool, with Telegram mapping it to Bot API entities or safe HTML.

options.title: Expose Telegram-Only Entities
options.body: Add a narrow Telegram-specific `entities` and `caption_entities` path with validation and focused delivery tests.

options.title: Keep HTML-Only Support
options.body: Declare `<tg-emoji>` HTML passthrough the supported custom emoji path for now and keep raw entity arrays out of the generic message tool.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Rich-Text Entity API
recommendation.body: Add a typed representation that can carry custom emoji IDs through the shared message tool, with Telegram mapping it to Bot API entities or safe HTML.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest routing signal from the prior review on this issue and current blame/history on both the Telegram send path and shared message-tool schema.
